How transit in the Tahoe Region is paid for, route by route

This model brings the region's transit operating costs and funding sources into one place, with the goal of providing transparency and showing the trade-offs of future funding options.

This tool is a draft undergoing further review and stakeholder validation.

Today

Existing funding conditions

A snapshot of how all transit operating revenue sources are currently budgeted in fiscal year (FY) 26-27.

Inputs users can change

Inputs, assumptions, and rules

These pages allow users to edit service hours, operating cost rates, funding amounts, model assumptions, and how each funding source is split across routes. Use the Reset button in the top right corner to reset to original inputs.

Results and future

One-year and five-year outlooks

The One-year outlook shows the balance for a selected fiscal year by route, agency, and jurisdiction. The Five-year outlook projects each agency's balance through FY 30-31. The Agreements and risk page lists funding agreements and time-limited funds. All three pages update as users change inputs and assumptions.

Reference

Sources and notes

Includes every source file, numbered to match the superscripts throughout the model. The data notes and open questions flag known data issues and items that need partner validation.

A Snapshot of Today's Transit Funding Landscape

Transit funding in the Tahoe Region is complicated, with about 60 revenue sources and four transit providers. This page shows an overview of how transit is currently paid for, by operator, by route, and by funding source. This page is a draft, and inputs require further stakeholder validation.

Cost and revenue by agency

Revenue each agency receives, by funding level, against the cost of the services it runs. Hatched federal funds exceed the federal share cap and have no eligible operating use.

Costs from the costs tab2. Revenue from the FY 26-27 budgets1.

Revenue by funding level

FY 25-26 amounts budgeted for operations in the fact sheets, against the FY 26-27 budgets. Lighter bars show FY 25-26 fact sheet amounts. Solid bars show FY 26-27 budgets.

FY 25-26 from the fact sheets5,6,7,8. FY 26-27 from the financial plan1. Sources without a fact sheet amount count as zero in FY 25-26.

Where the money goes

Funding level, then the agency that receives it, then the service it is applied to, using the draft shares in the financial plan.

Hover a band for its amount. Draft shares from the Revenue %s tab1.

Scenario presets

Check a preset to apply it. Uncheck it to return those values to the source data. The effect line compares each preset with the source data for FY 26-27 and FY 30-31.

Model assumptions

Opening balance carried into FY 26-27

Enter each agency's FY 25-26 ending operating reserve if known. Leave at $0 to start from the FY 26-27 budget alone.

Services and operating costs

Annual cost is vehicle service hours (VSH) times the operator's cost per hour, unless a cost is entered directly. Urban and rural classes drive FTA 5307 and 5311 eligibility. Service type drives ADA rules.

InputChanged from source Add service CSV

Passenger trips, VSH, VSM, data year, and route conditions from the costs tab2. The Main Line subtotal is not counted; its three segments are. Financial plan reference cost from the T2-4 route cost model and the TNT/TMA FY 26-27 budget1.

Private and non-federalized operators. Add ski, resort, or airport shuttles with "Federalized" unchecked to see them in the regional picture. The model blocks federal funds from them.

Operator cost rates

Fully allocated operating cost per vehicle service hour and the annual escalator used for the five-year outlook.

VRH Rates tab, column J and notes2.

Jurisdiction shares by service

Share of each service attributed to each jurisdiction. These set the California and Nevada portions used by state-restricted sources, cap jurisdiction-restricted sources, and drive the jurisdiction results.

CSV

Defaults split each service equally among the jurisdictions in the costs tab "Local Route Conditions" column2. Lake Link is one-third Douglas County and two-thirds City of South Lake Tahoe, following the even zone split in the Operating Stats tab1. The SSTMA working model averages shares of miles, hours, stops, and ridership4.

Service plan elements

Recommended changes from the financial plan, with their annual marginal cost. Check "Include" to add one to the scenario. It then appears as a service users can fund on Allocation and rules.

Revenue projections by source

InputChanged from sourceCSV

Table A1 and Table A2 notes1. FTA growth 1 percent per year. TDA follows RTP projected population change (0.025 percent per year).

FTA 5307 sub-allocation between TTD and Placer County

The Lake Tahoe urbanized area (UZA) apportionment is split by an earned-share formula: the average of each operator's share of urban revenue miles, population, and ridership. 75 percent of 5307 goes to operations.

FTA Allocation Split (26-27) tab1. FY 27 values are the FY 25-26 apportionment plus 1 percent, marked "EXAMPLE" in the source.
